To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

varicella-zostervirus antigens suitable for complement-fixation or precipitation tests in the sera of patients suspected of having chickenpox or herpes zoster can be prepared readily in human amnion tissue cultures.
varicella-zostervirus antigens suitable for serological tests can be produced in human amnion tissue cultures.
varicella-zos-ter virus antigens suitable for complement-fixation and precipitation tests can be prepared from tissue cultures infected with the virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of varicella virus from vesicular lesions and from the blood of persons with chickenpox or with zoster.
the development and use of tissue culture antigen in the serological diagnosis of chickenpox and herpes zoster.
the preparation of a soluble antigen from a human amnion culture infected with varicella-zos-ter virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the soluble antigens of V-ZV are present in the culture fluids of infected amnion cells, that these antigens are capable of fixing complement with the sera of convalescent cases of varicella and zoster, and that the antigens of V- ZV are capable of precipitating with the sera of cases of zoster but not of varicella.

the antigens of var. zoster virus produced in human amnion tissue culture have proved suitable for use in the complement-fixation test, but that the precipitating antigens are not yet sufficiently well characterized for routine tests.
the antigens of variecella-zoster virus are soluble and that they are not identical with the virus particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soluble antigens of V-Z virus produced in tissue cultures can be used for diagnostic tests for antibodies in the sera from patients with chickenpox or with zoster.
the soluble antigens of zostervaricela virus produced in tissue cultures are useful reagents for the diagnosis of chickenpox and zoster.
tissue culture antigens are suitable for the diagnosis of chickenpox and zoster and that they are more readily prepared than antigens from infected vesicle fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tissue culture antigens can be prepared which are suitable for routine tests.
tissue culture antigens are suitable for routine serological tests for varicella-zostervirus antibodies.
tissue-culture antigen can be prepared from infected amnion cells in the same manner as from infected chick embryo or human diploid cell cultures.
